abstract: Maturation of replication-dependent histone pre-mRNA transcripts involves a 3' cleavage event facilitated by the conserved stem-loop binding protein (SLBP). Cellular conditions that trigger an error in this process are not well understood. Here, we developed a GFP-based in vivo histone 3' misprocessing reporter in Caenorhabditis elegans and performed a genome-wide RNAi screen for histone regulators. We found that depletion of genes involved in various steps of ribosomal RNA (rRNA) biosynthesis triggers misprocessing of histone 3' tail, with the strongest effect observed upon depletion of rpoa-2 encoding the core subunit of RNA polymerase I. Transcriptome sequencing reveals rpoa-2 knockdown mirrors the effect of depleting the C. elegans SLBP homologue CDL-1 at the protein level, indicating that rpoa-2 and CDL-1 co-regulate similar transcriptome targets. Depletion of rpoa-2 impairs endomitosis of the C. elegans intestinal cells and is accompanied by aberrant activation of cell cycle markers in the absence of change in DNA content. Gene interaction analysis shows that rpoa-2 signals through multiple conserved cell cycle regulators, including ATM-1, GEN-1, and LIN-35 to trigger histone misprocessing in both CDL-1 dependent and independent manners. Together, our findings reveal that disruption in the rRNA biogenesis pathway triggers histone misprocessing through conserved genome surveillance pathway regulators.
